text: Mostly because everyone's schedule is different now. Parents often work late, teenagers have classes or training in the evening, and it's easy to eat something quickly in front of a screen. I think it's a real loss, because shared meals are one of the few natural moments for talking without a specific reason. Even two or three meals together a week can make a difference.

tips.ru: Even two or three meals … a week — решение без максимализма.

questions.question: Why do some families no longer eat meals together?

text: Families have become smaller, especially in cities. My grandparents grew up with six or seven brothers and sisters, whereas most of my friends have just one or two. Roles have changed too — both parents usually work, and fathers are much more involved in bringing up children than they used to be. At the same time, respect for older relatives is still very strong.

tips.en: My grandparents … whereas most of my friends … compares through the speaker’s own family.

tips.ru: My grandparents … whereas most of my friends … — сравнение через свою семью.

tips.kk: At the same time … still very strong — өзгеріс пен дәстүрдің теңгерімі.
tips.ru: At the same time … still very strong — баланс перемен и традиций.

questions.question: How are families in your country different from families fifty years ago?

text: Both have advantages. In a large family you learn to share, negotiate and look after others from an early age, and there's always someone to play with. On the other hand, parents in a small family can give each child more attention and often more opportunities, like extra classes. I grew up with two brothers, so I'm probably biased towards bigger families.

tips.en: In a large family … On the other hand … gives a balanced comparison.
tips.kk: In a large family … On the other hand … — теңгерімді салыстыру.
tips.ru: In a large family … On the other hand … — сбалансированное сравнение.
tips.example: On the other hand, parents in a small family

tips.en: I'm probably biased shows maturity by admitting a personal view.
tips.kk: I'm probably biased — өз ұстанымын мойындау салиқалы естіледі.
tips.ru: I'm probably biased — признание своей позиции звучит зрело.
tips.example: I'm probably biased towards bigger families

questions.question: Is it better to grow up in a large family or a small one?

text: In Kazakhstan they usually do, and I think it works well in many families. Grandparents have time, patience and experience, and children learn traditions and the language from them. The difficulty comes when grandparents and parents disagree about rules, for example about sweets or screen time. It helps if the parents make the main decisions and the grandparents support them rather than compete.

tips.kk: In Kazakhstan they usually do — нақты тәжірибеден жауап.

questions.question: Should grandparents play a big role in raising children?

text: Some probably will, especially the ones that take a lot of time or money, like very big celebrations. But I don't think traditions will disappear; they'll just change form. My cousins living abroad join our family gatherings by video call, which would have seemed strange ten years ago. As long as people want to feel they belong somewhere, family traditions will find a way to continue.
